surface_mechanism_description: Tungsten nucleation on oxide surfaces occurs at hydroxyl sites generated by piranha sample preparation. Surface hydroxyls facilitate WF6 adsorption, while physisorbed water delays nucleation. SiH4 pre-exposure forms a reducing Si layer, promoting tungsten nucleation. WF6 reacts with oxide surfaces to form metal fluorides, which can be volatile or non-volatile, affecting etching and nucleation.
evidence: The text discusses the role of surface hydroxyl groups in tungsten nucleation, the reaction of WF6 with oxide surfaces to form metal fluorides, and the impact of SiH4 pre-exposure on forming a reducing Si layer. It also mentions the formation of volatile and non-volatile metal fluorides and their effect on etching and nucleation.
